## Target estimands

```{r}
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(broom)
library(causalworkshop)
propensity_model <- glm(
  net ~ income + health + temperature,
  family = binomial(),
  data = net_data
)
```

### *Average Treatment Effect (ATE)*

$$\tau = E[Y(1) - Y(0)]$$

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig.height: 2.0
set.seed(10)
p <- tibble(
  x = c(runif(10, 0, 0.9), runif(10, 0.1, 1)),
  y = rep(c(1, 0), each = 10),
  col = rep(c("Treated", "Control"), each = 10)
)
set.seed(10)
ggplot(p, aes(x = x, y = y, color = col)) +
  geom_text(aes(label = col), position = "jitter") + 
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        axis.text = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks = element_blank()) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("cornflower blue", "orange")) +
  labs(x = "", y = "")
```

## Matching in R (ATT)

```{r}
#| output-location: fragment
#| code-line-numbers: "|2|3-4|"
library(MatchIt)
m <- matchit(
  net_num ~ income + health + temperature,
  data = net_data
)
m
```

## Matching in R (ATT)

```{r}

matched_data <- get_matches(m, id = "i")
as_tibble(matched_data)
```

## Matching in R (ATM)

```{r}
#| code-line-numbers: "|4-5"
#| output-location: slide
m <- matchit(
  net_num ~ income + health + temperature,
  data = net_data,
  link = "linear.logit",
  caliper = 0.1
)
m
```

. . .

The caliper is the largest difference between two observations we accept as a match, measured in standard deviations of the propensity score (here, on the linear logit scale). Observations that cannot be matched within it are discarded

## Matching in R (ATM)

```{r}
matched_data <- get_matches(m, id = "i")
as_tibble(matched_data)
```

## Matching or weighting?

* Weighting is statistically more efficient; we recommend it when possible
* Matching has a distinct advantage: it's easy to understand
* Not everyone will follow a pseudo-population or a non-integer sample size

## Histogram of propensity scores

```{r}
#| include: false
library(propensity)
df <- propensity_model |>
  augment(type.predict = "response", data = net_data) |>
  mutate(
    w_ate = wt_ate(.fitted, net),
    w_att = wt_att(.fitted, net),
    w_atu = wt_atu(.fitted, net),
    w_atm = wt_atm(.fitted, net),
    w_ato = wt_ato(.fitted, net),
    net = factor(net)
  )
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
library(halfmoon)
ggplot(df, aes(.fitted)) + 
  geom_mirror_histogram(bins = 50, aes(group = net)) + 
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, lwd = 0.5) +
  ylab("count") + 
  xlab("propensity score") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = abs) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Tilting functions {background-color="#23373B"}

```{r}
#| include: false
tilt_df <- tibble(p = seq(0.01, 0.99, by = 0.01)) |>
  mutate(
    ATE = 1,
    ATT = p,
    ATU = 1 - p,
    ATM = pmin(p, 1 - p),
    ATO = p * (1 - p)
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(-p, names_to = "estimand", values_to = "tilt") |>
  mutate(
    tilting = tilt,
    treated = tilt / p,
    untreated = tilt / (1 - p)
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    c(tilting, treated, untreated),
    names_to = "panel",
    values_to = "value"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    panel = factor(
      panel,
      levels = c("tilting", "treated", "untreated"),
      labels = c(
        "tilting function",
        "weights (treated)",
        "weights (untreated)"
      )
    )
  )

plot_tilt <- function(.estimand) {
  tilt_df |>
    filter(estimand == .estimand) |>
    ggplot(aes(p, value)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) +
    facet_wrap(~panel, scales = "free_y") +
    labs(x = "propensity score", y = NULL) +
    expand_limits(y = 0)
}
```

Every weight is the ATE weight times a **tilting function**, $h(p_i)$

$$\Large w_i = \frac{h(p_i)Z_i}{p_i} + \frac{h(p_i)(1-Z_i)}{1 - p_i}$$

The tilting function reshapes the population we are targeting

## Target estimands: ATE {background-color="#23373B"}

Average Treatment Effect (ATE)

$$\Large w_{ATE} = \frac{Z_i}{p_i} + \frac{1-Z_i}{1 - p_i}$$

```{r}
#| eval: false
(Z / p) + ((1 - Z) / (1 - p))
```

The tilting function is $h(p_i) = 1$: the population is unchanged and the weights are unbounded

## ATE tilting function

```{r}
#| echo: false
plot_tilt("ATE")
```

## ATE

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
ggplot(df, aes(.fitted)) + 
  geom_mirror_histogram(bins = 50, aes(group = net)) + 
  geom_mirror_histogram(bins = 50, aes(fill = net, weight = w_ate), alpha = 0.5) + 
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, lwd = 0.5) +
  ylab("count") + 
  xlab("propensity score") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = abs) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("green", "blue")) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Target estimands: ATT & ATU {background-color="#23373B"}

. . .

Average Treatment Effect Among the Treated (ATT) $$\Large w_{ATT} = \frac{p_i Z_i}{p_i} + \frac{p_i (1-Z_i)}{1-p_i}$$

```{r}
#| eval: false
((p * Z) / p) + ((p * (1 - Z)) / (1 - p))
```

The tilting function is $h(p_i) = p_i$: the treated get a weight of 1

## Target estimands: ATT & ATU {background-color="#23373B"}

Average Treatment Effect Among the Unexposed (ATU) $$\Large w_{ATU} = \frac{(1-p_i)Z_i}{p_i} + \frac{(1-p_i)(1-Z_i)}{(1-p_i)}$$

```{r}
#| eval: false
(((1 - p) * Z) / p) + (((1 - p) * (1 - Z)) / (1 - p))
```

The tilting function is $h(p_i) = 1 - p_i$: the untreated get a weight of 1

## ATT

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
ggplot(df, aes(.fitted)) + 
  geom_mirror_histogram(bins = 50, aes(group = net)) + 
  geom_mirror_histogram(bins = 50, aes(fill = net, weight = w_att), alpha = 0.5) + 
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, lwd = 0.5) +
  ylab("count") + 
  xlab("propensity score") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = abs) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("green", "blue")) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## ATU

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
ggplot(df, aes(.fitted)) + 
  geom_mirror_histogram(bins = 50, aes(group = net)) + 
  geom_mirror_histogram(bins = 50, aes(fill = net, weight = w_atu), alpha = 0.5) + 
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, lwd = 0.5) +
  ylab("count") + 
  xlab("propensity score") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = abs) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("green", "blue")) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Target estimands: ATM & ATO {background-color="#23373B"}

. . .

Average Treatment Effect Among the Evenly Matchable (ATM) $$\Large w_{ATM} = \frac{\min \{p_i, 1-p_i\}}{Z_ip_i + (1-Z_i)(1-p_i)}$$

```{r}
#| eval: false
pmin(p, 1 - p) / (Z * p + (1 - Z) * (1 - p))
```

The tilting function is $h(p_i) = \min \{p_i, 1-p_i\}$: a triangle peaking at 0.5

## Target estimands: ATM & ATO {background-color="#23373B"}

Average Treatment Effect Among the Overlap Population $$\Large w_{ATO} = (1-p_i)Z_i + p_i(1-Z_i)$$

```{r}
#| eval: false
(1 - p) * Z + p * (1 - Z)
```

The tilting function is $h(p_i) = p_i(1-p_i)$: smooth, peaking at 0.5, and the weights are bounded by 0 and 1

## ATO tilting function

```{r}
#| echo: false
plot_tilt("ATO")
```

| Estimand | Target population  | Example Research Question |
|----------|--------------------|---------------------------|
| ATO     | Overlap population | *Same as ATM*             |

## ATE in R ![](img/hex/propensity.png){.absolute top="0" right="0" width="140"}

<br />

Average Treatment Effect (ATE) $w_{ATE} = \frac{Z_i}{p_i} + \frac{1-Z_i}{1 - p_i}$

```{r}
#| code-line-numbers: "|4"
library(propensity)
df <- propensity_model |>
  augment(type.predict = "response", data = net_data) |>
  mutate(w_ate = wt_ate(.fitted, net))
```

## Extreme weights

* The minimum of the ATE weights is 1, but the maximum is unbounded
* The closer the probability of the observed exposure is to 0, the higher the weight
* **Extreme weights** *destabilize* our estimate, resulting in worse precision and potentially worse bias

## Extreme weights

```{r}
#| output-location: slide
df |>
  arrange(desc(w_ate)) |>
  select(net, income, health, temperature, .fitted, w_ate)
```

## Stabilized weights ![](img/hex/propensity.png){.absolute top="0" right="0" width="140"}

```{r}
#| output-location: fragment
#| code-line-numbers: "|3"
df <- df |>
  mutate(
    sw_ate = wt_ate(.fitted, net, stabilize = TRUE)
  )

df |>
  summarize(mean = mean(sw_ate), min = min(sw_ate), max = max(sw_ate))
```

. . .

Stabilizing puts the marginal probability of the observed exposure in the numerator: the proportion exposed for exposed units, the proportion unexposed for unexposed units

## Trimming and truncation

* **Trimming**: set an acceptable range of the propensity score and drop the observations outside it
* **Truncation**: set the values outside the range to the minimum or maximum of the range
* Some authors use these terms interchangeably, or with the opposite meanings

## Trimming and truncation in R ![](img/hex/propensity.png){.absolute top="0" right="0" width="140"}

```{r}
#| output-location: slide
#| code-line-numbers: "|3-4|5|6"
df <- df |>
  mutate(
    trimmed_ps = ps_trim(.fitted, method = "adaptive") |>
      ps_refit(propensity_model),
    trimmed = is_unit_trimmed(trimmed_ps),
    trunc_ps = ps_trunc(.fitted, method = "pctl", lower = 0.01, upper = 1)
  )

df |>
  select(net, income, health, temperature, .fitted, trimmed) |>
  filter(trimmed)
```

## Trimming and truncation

* Trimming and truncation, like using a caliper, change the population we are making inferences about
* The tilting function is 0 for the observations we trimmed and 1 for the ones that remain
* You can think of the resulting estimand as another type of overlap population
